batch: r3 pass1-b (entries 620, 621, 624, 625, 636, 643, 651), first run 2026-10-01, independently re-verified 2026-10-04
summary: Seven entries verified (first run 2026-10-01, then every load-bearing claim re-checked on 2026-10-04 with fresh fetches: all file hashes, link states, mastheads, scan readings and counts reproduced; corrections are listed at the end of this summary) with real fetches (honest User-Agent Gettysburg-sources-QC, robots.txt read per host, at most 1 request/second/host, no browser, nothing under legacy/ or the other workflow's paths; working files only under tmp/sources-v2/r3b/). Verdicts: 5 APPROVE (620, 621, 624, 625, 636; all tier A2 so a rights review precedes any quoting), 2 APPROVE-LINKOUT-ONLY (643, 651; collection and index pages, tier C), 0 NEEDS-HUMAN-REVIEW, 0 REJECT. Link state of the listed URLs: 5 dead (620, 621, 624, 625 all 404 after the Dickinson Archives migration; 636 redirects to the Valley of the Shadow home page), 2 live (643, 651). Replacements fetched and matched: 620 and 624 now live at archives.dickinson.edu/document-descriptions/<same slug> (the 624 PDF is byte-identical to the Wayback copy); 621 and 625 exist only as Wayback captures (not found on the new site at the slugs tried); 636's PDF is at api.valley.newamericanhistory.org/storage/data/newspapers_pdfs/... (byte-identical to the 2024-09-17 Wayback capture of the old URL). Findings that matter: (1) Dickinson's typed transcripts misread the manuscripts: 624 reads Thursday where the handwriting says Tuesday (changes the chronology), 620 has at least four misreads in the war-news paragraph, so quote from the scans; (2) 620 is second-hand (the writer left Carlisle before the occupation) and 621 is a 1930 recollection that is largely second-hand and contradicted by entry 625 on whether Conway Hillman was in Carlisle at the first shell; (3) 625 is an unsigned Sentinel reporter's piece quoting Johnson, not an article by Johnson, and its date (June 1924) rests on archive metadata and a handwritten note; (4) 651 is the War Years index only, not 'all' Franklin County papers (the Eve of War and Aftermath indexes list collections it omits); (5) 643 holds eleven letters (F6500-F6509 in War Years plus F6510 of April 1865 under Aftermath), not ten. Not verified: the death dates of Chenoweth (father) and Hillman (rights inference only), the Sentinel issue that carries 625, Dickinson's own reuse terms (none found; the Citation Guide page has none), the 10 Stouffer letters beyond title, date and summary (two read in part), and anything on hosts that block or hide behind a challenge: www.loc.gov answered with a Cloudflare 'Just a moment' challenge (not circumvented) and panewsarchive.psu.edu robots.txt reset the connection (not fetched), so no Library of Congress or Pennsylvania Newspaper Archive text of the Franklin Repository was read; hd.housedivided.dickinson.edu sets Crawl-delay 600 and was not fetched beyond its robots.txt. CORRECTIONS from the 2026-10-04 re-check: (a) 643 relevance raised to campaign-and-battle because Amos Stouffer's 1863 diary (FD5500) records a visit to the Gettysburg field on 7-8 July and the cemetery dedication (the first run called the diary hearsay only); (b) 620's typed transcript has two more deviations from the scan (exams for exercises; July for Sept.); (c) 621: the earlier-capture truncation is consistent with Wayback CDX sizes, and today the page's own PDF link resolves to the complete 2024-05-19 capture, but cite that capture explicitly; Hillman was alive in 1923 and 1925 per Dickinson's alumni-magazine index, and that index points to a published November 1923 Alumnus recollection by him (a lead, not read, and a possible tier A1 alternative). Still not verified: death dates of Chenoweth and Hillman (searched, not found), the Sentinel issue for 625, Dickinson's reuse terms, and any Franklin Repository text on hosts that block or challenge bots (loc.gov, panewsarchive.psu.edu: not fetched).
systemic_findings: Dickinson Archives migration: all four listed Dickinson links 404 (after a 301 to https). The new Drupal site keeps some items under /document-descriptions/<same slug> (620 and 624 resolve with 200 and byte-identical or near-identical PDFs under /sites/default/files/files_document/), but 621 and 625 do not resolve at the slugs tried and are not on the people pages read (an earlier reviewer found 587 also absent). Remaining dead Dickinson entries are worth testing at /document-descriptions/<slug> before falling back to Wayback.

Wayback PDF captures can be truncated: the captures of the 621 PDF up to 2024-04-16 and of the 624 PDF up to 2023-12-09 are cut at about 1 MiB and will not open (pdftotext: Couldn't read xref table). The CDX list (web.archive.org/cdx/search/cdx?url=...&fl=timestamp,statuscode,length) shows a complete later capture (621: 2024-05-19, 6,058,284 bytes; 624: 2024-03-29, 4,617,670 bytes). Dickinson's typed transcripts are not reliable enough to quote without the scan: 624 turns Tuesday into Thursday; 620 reads 'And Army' for 'Our Army', 'now has just announced' for 'News has just arrived' and 'Our force feels' for 'Our prospects were'.

Valley of the Shadow moved: valley.lib.virginia.edu now 301-redirects every path to the new site's home page (a dead link in disguise). The newspaper PDFs and TEI files live at api.valley.newamericanhistory.org/storage/data/newspapers_pdfs/<paper+year>/<file>.pdf and .../newspapers/<paper+year>/<file>.xml (verified on one issue by identical sha256 with a Wayback capture of the old URL), item pages at valley.newamericanhistory.org/newspapers/<paper>/<yyyy>/<mm>/<dd>, letters at /papers/F<id>, diaries at /diaries/FD<id>. The same remapping should be tested for the other valley.lib.virginia.edu entries (Part X and XI). The site states free non-commercial use only and carries a CC BY-NC 4.0 badge, so its transcriptions and summaries are not reusable commercially.

Part headers are loose: Part IX says 'compiled by Dickinson College House Divided Project' but the four items are hosted by Dickinson Archives & Special Collections (the pages' own footer); Part X says sources 'cited by the House Divided Project' for a newspaper PDF hosted by the Valley of the Shadow. Treat the part labels as editorial, not as provenance.

items.written: 1863-07-15 (dateline Lewistown, Pa.; contemporaneous, 14 days after the shelling of Carlisle; second-hand, the writer was away from Carlisle during the occupation)
items.rights_basis: Unpublished 1863 manuscript letter by an adult whose sons were at college in 1863, so he cannot plausibly have lived past 1955 and the life+70 term has expired (inference: his death date was not looked up). Host: the item page footer reads Copyright (c) 2020 (live page: 2025) Archives & Special Collections at Dickinson College, All rights reserved; the typed transcript is the Archives' own work; no reuse terms were found (the Citation Guide page has none). Tier A2: the letter text is public domain by date, the host's notice and transcription rights are unresolved. Quote from the manuscript scan, not the typed transcript.
items.evidence: Listed URL http://archives.dickinson.edu/civil-war-resources/letter-george-d-chenoweth-james-w-marshall: 301 to https, then 404 'Page not found | Archives & Special Collections' (archives.dickinson.edu/robots.txt, 200, disallows only admin, search, core and profile paths, so the fetches were allowed). The item moved with the site migration: https://archives.dickinson.edu/document-descriptions/letter-george-d-chenoweth-james-w-marshall returns 200 with the same title, 5 pages, date July 15 1863, location I-Original-1863-4. Its PDF https://archives.dickinson.edu/sites/default/files/files_document/I-Original-1863-4_0.pdf returns 200, 5,137,337 bytes, sha256 a91e485a3fc457f2...; 5 pages: p1 cover sheet, p2-3 manuscript scans, p4-5 typed transcript with a text layer. Its text is identical to the Wayback copy of the old PDF (capture 2024-03-02, 5,137,633 bytes) except the cover header ('Civil War Resources' became 'Documents Online'). I viewed manuscript p3: signature G. D. Chenoweth, matches. Two description claims checked: (1) 'Carlisle civilian's account of the Confederate occupation': the letter, dated Lewistown July 15th 1863, says the family was driven out of Carlisle by the last train before the rebels entered, then reports twelve thousand rebels entering on a Saturday evening, officers camping by Dr. Johnson's door, men on the campus, stores plundered and a man arrested until he told where shoes were hidden; (2) it reports that after Harrisburg militia entered, rebel cavalry shelled the town overnight, a flag of truce went to Gen. Smith who refused, the Barracks and Gashouse were burned, a shell burst in Dr. Johnson's reading room and families took to cellars. Both hold. Cross-check: entry 624 (Griffith, an eyewitness, 3 July) agrees on the shelling, Smith's refusal and the burned garrison and gas house but estimates about 7,000 troops where Chenoweth says 12,000. Re-verified in a second run on 2026-10-04 with fresh fetches into a new cache (tmp/sources-v2/r3b-recheck/): the listed URL is still 301 then 404; the replacement item page is still 200 (title "Letter from George D. Chenoweth to James W. Marshall", 5 pages, July 15, 1863, I-Original-1863-4); the PDF re-downloaded as 5,137,337 bytes with the same sha256 prefix a91e485a3fc457f2; its text layer differs from the old Wayback PDF only in the cover line ("Civil War Resources" became "Documents Online"); I rendered manuscript sheet 3 again and read the signature "G. D. Chenoweth" and the war-news paragraph; the replacement page lists the live People tag "Chenoweth, George Durbin" and its own summary says he left Carlisle before the raid.
items.extraction_notes: pdf-text adapter on PDF pages 4-5 (about 4,300 characters of typed transcript: one long paragraph, salutation and closing). Then check every quoted line against the handwriting scans on p2-3 (image only). Segment into 3-4 passages: leaving Carlisle and the occupation, plunder and arrests, the shelling and cellars, news of Gettysburg, Vicksburg and the New York draft riots. Keep the writer's spelling. Replace the cover-sheet contact block with a provenance line: Dickinson College Archives & Special Collections, I-Original-1863-4. Use the live URL and PDF named above.
issues: Not an eyewitness account: he left Carlisle on the last train the Thursday before the rebels came and returned afterwards, so the occupation and shelling are reported second-hand; attribute accordingly.

Dickinson's typed transcript misreads the manuscript in the closing paragraphs (checked again on the scan 2026-10-04): 'And Army' for 'Our Army gained a complete victory over Lee at Gettysburg', 'now has just announced' for 'News has just arrived', 'Our force feels we're never so bright' for 'Our prospects were never so bright'; it also appears to read 'a form of the exams' where the hand reads 'a part of the exercises', and 'open as usual in July' where the hand appears to read 'in Sept.'. Quote from the scan, never from the typed transcript.

Weekday slip: he puts both the militia's arrival and the shelling on 'Tuesday evening'; Griffith (entry 624) and the Dickinson catalogue place the shelling on the evening of 1 July (a Wednesday). Do not take his weekdays as dates.

Writer identity: the old catalogue page tagged 'Chenoweth, George D.'; the live page tags 'Chenoweth, George Durbin' (a son, Dickinson class of 1868), but the letter names 'Durbin & Alexander' in the third person as freshmen, so the writer is the father, George Davenport Chenoweth (a Dickinson trustee per a Dickinson student blog, not an authoritative source). Do not attribute it to the son.
The listed URL is dead since the Dickinson Archives migration; cite the replacement.
Estimate of 'twelve thousand' is the writer's hearsay; do not use as a strength figure.

items.written: 1930-09-09 (dateline Ft. Worth, Texas; retrospective, 67 years after the events; largely second-hand, see issues)
items.rights_basis: Unpublished 1930 letter to the Dickinson president (Morgan Papers). The writer was in the class of 1873 (born about 1850-1853). The Dickinson alumni-magazine people page (fetched 2026-10-04) shows him active in the Nov 1923 and Nov 1925 issues, but no death date was found (two web searches returned none), so the life+70 term is inferred to have expired (he would have had to live beyond 1955, past about age 102) and the Morgan Papers donor terms are unknown. Host: item page footer Copyright (c) 2020 Archives & Special Collections at Dickinson College, All rights reserved; typed transcript is the Archives' work. Tier A2, not A1, because a 1930 unpublished work needs the death date checked.
items.evidence: Listed URL http://archives.dickinson.edu/civil-war-resources/letter-conway-w-hillman-james-h-morgan: 301 to https, then 404. https://archives.dickinson.edu/document-descriptions/letter-conway-w-hillman-james-h-morgan is also 404, and the item is not listed on the live people pages for Samuel D. Hillman or Herman M. Johnson, so the Wayback capture is the only copy found. Wayback item page, capture 2024-02-23 (200, 27,613 bytes): 'Letter from Conway W. Hillman to James H. Morgan', 14 pages, date September 9 1930, location Morgan Papers Box 3 Folder Hil-Hitchk (its 'Year: 1863' field is the subject year, not the letter's). The PDF that page links to (and every capture to 2024-04-16, about 1.0 MB each in the CDX listing) is cut off at 1,048,576 bytes and does not open; the capture of 2024-05-19 (web.archive.org/web/20240519184827if_/https://archives.dickinson.edu/sites/all/files/files_war/MorganPapers-1930-09-30.pdf) is complete: 6,058,284 bytes, sha256 67acb79a631cb8e5..., 14 pages: p1 cover sheet, p2-11 manuscript scans on Pan American Petroleum & Transport Co. letterhead, p12-14 typed transcript with a text layer (about 10,500 characters). I viewed p2: dateline 'Ft Worth, Sept 9/30', 'Dear Morgan', matching the transcript. Two description claims checked: (1) 'Prof. Samuel Hillman's son': the letter speaks of 'Father', a Carlisle Home Guard member who gave a barefoot rebel his boots; the catalogue page names Samuel Dickinson Hillman ('50, taught 1860-1874); (2) 'recollection of the summer of 1863': the first rebel occupation in late June (campus camp, East College as hospital, Old West guarded), then the shelling (he says about 300 shells; a fuse shell in South College; Dr. Johnson's recitation room hit). Both hold. Re-verified in a second run on 2026-10-04 with fresh fetches into a new cache (tmp/sources-v2/r3b-recheck/): the listed URL and the new-site slug (plus a '-0' variant and three guessed PDF paths under /sites/default/files/files_document/) are all 404, so no live copy on the migrated site was found; the Wayback item page (capture 2024-02-23) still gives 14 pages, September 9, 1930, Morgan Papers Box 3 and names Samuel Dickinson Hillman ('50) as the father; the complete PDF capture re-downloaded as 6,058,284 bytes, sha256 prefix 67acb79a631cb8e5, 14 pages; the typed transcript again shows the passages quoted above (the boots anecdote, 'About 300 shells', the mother and son away in New York, the Gov. Curtin telegram). The CDX index (web.archive.org/cdx/search/cdx?url=archives.dickinson.edu/sites/all/files/files_war/MorganPapers-1930-09-30.pdf&fl=timestamp,statuscode,length) lists captures 2019-11-12, 2022-05-21 and 2024-04-16 at about 1.01 MB each and the complete one of 2024-05-19 (5,990,827 bytes in the index): the earlier note that the older captures are truncated is consistent with those sizes (I did not open the old ones this time); on 2026-10-04 the item page's own PDF link resolved to the complete 2024-05-19 capture.
items.extraction_notes: pdf-text adapter on PDF p12-14 (typed transcript with a text layer); p2-11 are image-only scans for checking. Use only the 1863 passages: the occupation and camping and the boots anecdote (p12), the shelling and shell hits and the Gettysburg field (p12-13), the Home Guard addendum (end of p14). Drop the 1870 student rebellion, railroad litigation and personal paragraphs. Use the complete 2024-05-19 capture, not the page's own PDF link. The transcript carries the Archives' query marks ([Soders?], [Balshevic?], [Ease?]) and glitches ('<Df10s', 'Lout her', 'Weill am'); keep brackets or check against the scan.
issues: Retrospective (67 years) and largely second-hand: Hillman says he and his mother left Carlisle in early June and were in New York when the shelling happened; most of the account is his father's stories and hearsay (a telegram from Gov. Curtin, the Home Guard policing the Gettysburg field). Attribute as Hillman's 1930 recollection.

Contradicted by entry 625 (Johnson, Carlisle Sentinel, 1924), which has Johnson on the East College steps with 'my chum Conway Wing Hillman' when the first shell passed; Hillman's own letter puts him away. Do not use either to place Hillman in Carlisle on 1 July.
Details to check before use: 'Stuart's cavalry' as the shelling force, about 300 shells, 'a regiment or so of infantry' under Gen. Smith, three or four marked shell hits. None verified.
Date: the PDF file name says 1930-09-30 but the dateline and cover sheet say 9 September 1930.
Only about a third of the 14 pages concerns 1863; the rest is Dickinson alumni business and the 1870 student rebellion.

Listed link dead; only Wayback copies found. The CDX sizes show the captures before 2024-05-19 are about 1.0 MB (the earlier run could not open one), so cite the explicit capture web.archive.org/web/20240519184827if_/https://archives.dickinson.edu/sites/all/files/files_war/MorganPapers-1930-09-30.pdf rather than relying on whatever capture a Wayback redirect picks.

Lead, not read: the Dickinson alumni-magazine people page for Hillman (archives.dickinson.edu/dickinson-alumni-magazine-people/hillman-conway-wing, fetched) says the Dickinson Alumnus of November 1923 carries Hillman's recollections of the Confederate bombardment of Carlisle. A 1923 magazine imprint would be a pre-1931 published text (a candidate for tier A1 and a better quote source than this 1930 manuscript letter); it needs its own review. The same page lists a Hillman mention in the November 1925 issue.

items.written: 1863-07-03 (dateline Carlisle; contemporaneous eyewitness letter, two days after the shelling)
items.rights_basis: Unpublished 1863 letter by Thomas Miller Griffith (1834-1898 per Dickinson's own collection description of the Thomas Miller Griffith papers, fetched), so the life+70 term expired in 1968: the text is public domain. Host: item page footer Copyright (c) 2025 Archives & Special Collections at Dickinson College, All rights reserved; origin 'Gift of Thomas Miller Griffith's daughter and Sara Cochran Coppes'; the typed transcript is the Archives' work; no reuse terms found. Tier A2 pending a human look at the host's terms; quote from the manuscript scan.
items.evidence: Listed URL http://archives.dickinson.edu/civil-war-resources/letter-thomas-m-griffith-his-siblings: 301 to https, then 404. Live replacement https://archives.dickinson.edu/document-descriptions/letter-thomas-m-griffith-his-siblings returns 200 (found by testing the new path): same title, 9 pages, date July 3 1863, location MC 2005.4, B1, F2. Its PDF https://archives.dickinson.edu/sites/default/files/files_document/mc20005-04_b01f02.pdf returns 200, 4,617,670 bytes, sha256 057af021fa8f88b6..., byte-identical to the Wayback capture of 2024-03-29 of the old PDF. Do not confuse with /document-descriptions/letter-thomas-m-griffith-his-sister, a different letter (June 23 1857, MC 2005.4 B1 F1) that web searches surface. PDF layout: p1 cover sheet, p2-7 six manuscript scans, p8-9 typed transcript with a text layer (about 7,500 characters). I viewed manuscript p2 and p5: 'Carlisle, July 3, 1863 / Dear Bro. & Sister' and the passage on the rebels' departure; they match the transcript except for one misread (issues). Two description claims checked: (1) 'Carlisle civilian': a Methodist minister who lived beside the campus (a Confederate brigade camped in front of his window; he and other pastors declined to open their churches to the rebels) and who was handling college examinations; (2) 'letter on the invasion': it reports Jenkins's advance guard entering on a Saturday about ten o'clock and infantry that afternoon (he guesses about 7,000, 'perhaps you heard 30000'), Ewell at the garrison, requisitions paid in scrip, rebel chaplains preaching on the campus, 60 Union prisoners paroled on the square, and Fitz Hugh Lee's cavalry (about 2,000) shelling from about eight in the evening until three in the morning while Gen. Smith refused three flags of truce. Both hold. It agrees with entry 620 on the shelling and the burned garrison and gas house. Re-verified in a second run on 2026-10-04 with fresh fetches into a new cache (tmp/sources-v2/r3b-recheck/): the listed URL is still 404; the replacement page is 200 (9 pages, July 3, 1863, MC 2005.4 B1 F2, People tags Griffith, Johnson, Ewell, Jenkins, Fitzhugh Lee, Smith, Wilson); the PDF re-downloaded as 4,617,670 bytes with sha256 prefix 057af021fa8f88b6 and is byte-identical to the Wayback copy of the old PDF saved in the first run; I rendered manuscript sheet 4 (PDF p5) and read "They staid till Tuesday morning at 5" where the typed transcript says Thursday, and sheet 5 (PDF p6) which matches the typed shelling passage; the Griffith papers description page (fetched again) reads "Thomas Miller Griffith (1834-1898)".
items.extraction_notes: pdf-text adapter on PDF p8-9 (typed transcript with a text layer, about 7,500 characters); p2-7 are image-only handwriting for checking. The text layer renders every apostrophe and quotation mark as U+FFFD (o'clock, Dixie's Land): normalise before use. Segment by the letter's own paragraphs (about 8 passages: commencement and the rush home, the Saturday occupation, orderly conduct and requisitions, Sunday preaching and the churches, departure and prisoners, the evening shelling and Smith's refusals, damage and wounded). Fix the Tuesday/Thursday misread (issues) from the scan before quoting.
issues: The typed transcript says the rebels 'staid till Thursday morning at 5'; the manuscript (p5) reads Tuesday. A Thursday reading would contradict the letter's own sequence (prisoners on 'Tuesday forenoon', rebels gone the next morning). Quote from the scan or correct it.
The letter gives weekdays, not dates; the date of the shelling (1 July) comes from the catalogue description, not the letter, and should be cross-checked.
Troop estimates (about 7,000; 'perhaps you heard 30000 or more') are the writer's guesses; do not use as strength figures.
Writer is a Union-loyalist clergyman and says so (kept his church closed to avoid greeting the rebels); he is a civilian witness, not a neutral one.
The listed URL is dead since the Dickinson Archives migration; cite the replacement.

items.written: 1924-06 per the archive (clipping annotated 'From Sentinel, June 1924'); retrospective, about 61 years after the events; the text's round numbers (sixty years ago, fifty years since 1873) would also fit 1923
items.rights_basis: Published in a US newspaper in 1924 (archive metadata 'June 1924' plus a handwritten note on the clipping): a pre-1931 imprint, so public domain. Tier A2 rather than A1 because the only copy is Dickinson's scan of an undated, unpaged clipping (no masthead) carrying the host's notice Copyright (c) 2020 Archives & Special Collections at Dickinson College, All rights reserved, and the issue date was not confirmed from the Sentinel itself.
items.evidence: Listed URL http://archives.dickinson.edu/civil-war-resources/carlisle-sentinel-%E2%80%9Ctheodore-m-johnson-tells-civil-war-days-carlisle%E2%80%9D: 301 to https, then 404. On the live site /document-descriptions/ with the plain and the curly-quote slugs are both 404 and the item is not on the Herman M. Johnson people page (5 items), so only Wayback copies were found. Wayback item page, capture 2023-12-07 (200, 26,604 bytes): 'Carlisle Sentinel, Theodore M. Johnson Tells of Civil War Days in Carlisle', 2 pages, date June 1924, location I-Original-1924-2, format Newspapers and Magazines. PDF (capture 2024-02-25, 200, 725,723 bytes, sha256 22c26181c78861ad...): p1 cover sheet with text, p2 a single 781x4316 px JPEG of a newspaper clipping with no text layer. I read the whole clipping (six crops): kicker 'Member of Class of '73 here on a visit'; headline 'Theodore M. Johnson Tells of Civil War Days in Carlisle'; an unsigned Sentinel report on Theo. M. Johnson of Pittston, son of Dr. Herman M. Johnson, president of the college 1860-1868, in town for commencement; his quoted recollections: he was about nine; on the East College steps when the first shell crossed the town; a second shell hit a second-floor window, sixth from the east side; a third split a cherry tree and was a dud; Confederate cavalry came from the west a few days before the shelling and camped on the campus; his father gave the commander a Masonic sign and guards were put on the college buildings; the colonel and staff ate with the family with their own cooks. The entry's description, 'Recollection by the son of the Dickinson College president', holds on both points (son of the president; recollection of 1863). Re-verified in a second run on 2026-10-04 with fresh fetches into a new cache (tmp/sources-v2/r3b-recheck/): the listed URL is still 404, and two guessed paths for the item and two for the PDF on the live site are also 404; the Wayback PDF re-downloaded as 725,723 bytes with the same sha256 prefix 22c26181c78861ad; I read the six crops of the clipping again: kicker, headline, "Speaking to a Sentinel reporter, Mr. Johnson told of some of his recollections", "my chum Conway Wing Hillman", the cherry tree and the handwritten "From Sentinel, June 1924".
items.extraction_notes: Image only: no text layer, so the path is manual-transcription from the 781x4316 px JPEG in the 2024-02-25 PDF capture (about 700 words in 3-4 paragraphs of quotation inside the reporter's frame). Two or three passages: the shelling (first shell, East College window, cherry tree), the cavalry occupation and meals, the Copperheads remark. Keep the reporter's framing separate from Johnson's quoted words. A second person should check the transcription against the image.
issues: Authorship: an unsigned Sentinel reporter's piece quoting Johnson, not an article by Johnson; the entry's 'Theodore M. Johnson, Tells of Civil War Days in Carlisle' turns the headline into an author and a title. Cite as Carlisle Sentinel, June 1924, interview with Theodore M. Johnson.
Date and page unconfirmed: the clipping has no masthead, date line or page; 'June 1924' comes from the archive metadata and a handwritten note. Find the issue before citing a day.
Retrospective by a man who was about nine in 1863.

Dickinson's catalogue blurb says Johnson saw Rodes's division of Ewell's corps and Stuart's cavalry; the article names no unit or general (only 'Confederate cavalry'). Do not import the blurb's unit identifications.
Conflicts with entry 621: Johnson puts Conway Hillman beside him at the first shell; Hillman's 1930 letter has him in New York.
Listed link dead; no live replacement found.

items.written: 1863-07-08 (issue date read from the masthead; contemporaneous, one week after the battle)
items.rights_basis: A newspaper issue of 8 July 1863 (masthead read on the scan): public domain. The PDF is a facsimile hosted by the Valley of the Shadow. The site's Copyright and Fair Use Statement (valley.newamericanhistory.org/about/copyright, fetched) says much source material is public domain but some may still be under copyright, and offers the site free for non-commercial research, teaching, scholarship and private study; each page footer carries a Creative Commons BY-NC 4.0 badge link. The TEI transcription (tagged 1998) and the page summaries are the project's work. Tier A2: transcribe from the page images ourselves; do not reuse the host's transcription or summaries commercially.
items.evidence: Listed URL http://valley.lib.virginia.edu/newspapers_pdfs/fr1863/pa.fr.fr.1863.07.08.pdf: 301 to https, then 301 to https://valley.newamericanhistory.org/ (200, the site home page): the PDF is not served there any more (a dead link in disguise). The same file is at https://api.valley.newamericanhistory.org/storage/data/newspapers_pdfs/fr1863/pa.fr.fr.1863.07.08.pdf (200, 4,125,848 bytes, sha256 1d64c1a5a039127d...), byte-identical to the Wayback capture of the old URL from 2024-09-17. Robots: valley.newamericanhistory.org/robots.txt is 404 (no rules); the api host's says 'User-agent: * Disallow:' (allow all). The issue also has a page, https://valley.newamericanhistory.org/newspapers/franklin-repository/1863/07/08 (200, 397,198 bytes), with summaries, a transcription and links to the PDF and the TEI file (api...storage/data/newspapers/fr1863/pa.fr.fr.1863.07.08.xml, 145,920 bytes; header: Franklin Repository, Chambersburg, 1863-07-08, weekly, extent 08). The PDF has 8 pages, each a 3744x5184 px bitonal image (made with Photoshop in 2009), no text layer. I read the masthead on p1: 'The Franklin Repository', Vol. 70, Chambersburg, Pa., Wednesday July 8 1863, No. 24 (the weekday is partly torn). On p5 I saw the headlines 'The Invasion! The Whole Rebel Army in Franklin County! 47,000 pass through Chambersburg! ... Eleven Days of Rebel Occupation in Force!' next to 'Vicksburg Taken!'. So the description holds on two points: it is the Chambersburg paper of that date, and it reports eleven days of occupation. The issue also holds an account of Jenkins's first raid (p1), Gettysburg dispatches (p4-5) and Vicksburg. items.evidence: Listed URL https://valley.newamericanhistory.org/war/letters-and-diaries/franklin/stouffer returns 200 (155,024 bytes), title 'Letters of the Stouffer Family - The War Years - The Valley of the Shadow'; heading 'Stouffer Family (1861-1865)'. The page's tab counts read War 12, Aftermath 1, and its embedded data lists letters F6500 to F6509 (ten) and diaries FD7001 (Eliza R. Stouffer, 1863) and FD5500 (Amos Stouffer, 1863); the Franklin index (entry 651) says 'ten wartime letters (1861-1865)' plus the two 1863 diaries, which is the entry's wording. I fetched all ten letter pages (200): dated 20 Dec 1861 to 17 Aug 1864; F6506 is Jacob Stouffer to his daughter Mary, 5 July 1863, describing the rebel army camping around his farm, Lee's headquarters in Shetter's woods and the wagon trains and artillery marching toward Gettysburg on 30 June. The Aftermath tab adds an eleventh letter, F6510 (Benjamin Stouffer to Emma, 16 April 1865). Diaries read: FD5500 has daily entries for 1863 including the rebels in Franklin County from 15 June, hearsay of the Gettysburg battle on 3-5 July, and a trip to the cemetery dedication on 18-20 November; FD7001 is Eliza's trip diary of 12 June to 10 July 1863 in Lancaster County with rumours of the invasion and no battle text. The entry's description (ten family letters plus the 1863 diaries of Amos and Eliza) therefore matches the host's own count; the collection holds eleven letters if the Aftermath item is counted. Re-verified in a second run on 2026-10-04 with fresh fetches into a new cache (tmp/sources-v2/r3b-recheck/): the page is still 200 with the same ten letter ids F6500 to F6509 and diary ids FD5500 and FD7001, tab counts War 12 and Aftermath 1 (page weight differs between fetches, 155,024 bytes on 2026-10-01 against 44,440 on 2026-10-04, with the same ids and text); F6500 is Eliza R. Stouffer to Anna Hoover, December 20, 1861, F6509 is Eliza R. Stouffer to her 'Sister in Faith,' August 17, 1864, and the Aftermath page lists F6510 (Benjamin Stouffer to Emma V. Stouffer, April 16, [1865]); F6506 (Jacob Stouffer to Mary R. Stouffer, July 5, 1863) was re-read and does say the rebels entered Chambersburg on 15 June, Lee had his headquarters in A. Shetter's woods and about 700 army wagons passed toward Gettysburg on Tuesday 30 June. CORRECTION to the first run: the diary of Amos Stouffer (FD5500, re-read this run) is not only hearsay: after rumours of the battle on 3 to 5 July it records on Tuesday 7 July 1863 that he went to the battlefield (he got there about 11 o'clock and saw a great many unburied rebels and some Union soldiers), on 8 July that he went all over the battle field, and on 18 to 20 November the trip to the cemetery dedication. So the collection reaches the battle only through hearsay and a post-battle visit; there is still no eyewitness account of the fighting. The relevance field is therefore raised from campaign-only to campaign-and-battle.

items.evidence: Listed URL https://valley.newamericanhistory.org/war/letters-and-diaries/franklin returns 200 (199,369 bytes), title 'Letters & Diaries: Franklin County, PA - The War Years - The Valley of the Shadow'. It lists 27 named collections plus 'Additional Personal Papers Collections' (22 items), each with a summary and an item count (for example Bitner 22, Demus and Christy 67, Stevens 13, Stouffer 12). The sister pages /eve/letters-and-diaries/franklin (6 collections) and /aftermath/letters-and-diaries/franklin (9), both 200, include collections the War Years page lacks: Abraham Essick, Edward McPherson and the Wills and Estates Collection (Eve), Jubal Early and David Hafer (Aftermath).
